newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIRS raises estimate for 1996/97 French sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: FIRS raises estimate for 1996/97 French sugar crop.

text.p: French sugar intervention board FIRS now expects a 1996/97 beet sugar crop of "at least" 4.05 million tonnes instead of the 3.97 million it predicted last month, a FIRS official told Reuters.
But this would still represent a decline from a final 4.199 million tonnes of beet sugar produced in 1995/96.
The new estimate would assume a national sugar yield of 9.60 tonnes per hectare against a previous target of 9.40 tonne and a yield of 9.77 tonnes last year, the official said.
Crop area is expected to fall to 422,000 hectares from 430,000 last year.
In its October report, FIRS said initial data collected since beet processing started in late September suggested 1996/97 sugar production may exceed the 3.97 million tonnes it forecast last month.
"Contrary to what was expected, rain at the end of August and in early September increased plant weight without sharply cutting sugar content," FIRS said in the report.
